question: How can model-based methods (planning: DP, heuristic search) and model-free learning (MC, TD) be unified, and how should planning computation be distributed?
hypothesis: Planning and learning share one structure (value updates backed up from experience, simulated or real), so they can be intermixed and differ mainly in update type, order and retention.
contributions: Unified view: all state-space planning is value updates on simulated experience
Dyna architecture: acting, model-learning, direct RL and planning together
Treatment of wrong models and exploration (Dyna-Q+)
Focusing of updates: prioritized sweeping, trajectory sampling, RTDP
Decision-time planning: heuristic search, rollouts, MCTS

limits: All methods are tabular; function approximation is deferred to Part II.
Dyna-Q's model assumes a deterministic environment (Exercise 8.5 asks for the stochastic extension).
Trajectory-sampling results hold for randomly generated tasks only; authors say 'not conclusive'.
The RTDP comparison is one racetrack; authors say 'not definitive'.
Expected-vs-sample analysis assumes equally likely successors and correct successor values (Exercise 8.6 asks about skew).
Several experiments are quoted from Sutton 1990, Peng and Williams 1993, Moore and Atkeson 1993; n, kappa, theta and seed counts for the changing-maze runs are not given.
No numbers are printed for MCTS or rollout performance beyond the Go sentence.
practices: Give each Dyna step n planning updates after acting, model-learning and direct RL; more planning steps cut episodes needed (Sec 8.2).
Use an exploration bonus on simulated rewards (kappa*sqrt(tau)) when the environment can change (Sec 8.3).
Prioritise planning updates by size of change and work backward to predecessors (Sec 8.4).
Prefer sample updates when branching is large and states are many; expected updates win only if there is time to finish them (Sec 8.5).
Distribute updates by on-policy trajectory sampling on large problems with few relevant states (Sec 8.6-8.7).
Use decision-time planning when latency allows; otherwise plan in the background and act from a stored policy (Sec 8.8).
In MCTS use a tree policy (epsilon-greedy or UCB) inside the tree and a cheap rollout policy outside (Sec 8.11).

terms.definition: Models that produce a description of all possibilities and their probabilities
Models that produce just one of the possibilities, sampled according to the probabilities
any computational process that takes a model as input and produces or improves a policy for interacting with the modeled environment
Real experience improving value/policy directly (direct RL), improving the model (model-learning); value improvement via the model is indirect RL
the process that selects the starting states and actions for the simulated experiences generated by the model
Background: simulated experience gradually improves a policy or value function. Decision-time: planning starts after each new state and outputs one action, results usually discarded
the fixed policy used to simulate trajectories in rollout algorithms and outside the tree in MCTS
informed policy that selects actions inside the MCTS tree, balancing exploration and exploitation
